story.head: Nichushkin meets his old team
paras: The Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday, while the Blue Jackets (5-6-0) lost 3-2 to Carolina on Thursday. The Avalanche played last night, and the Blue Jackets are rested. Going in, the Avalanche are third in the Central (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Jackets seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th).

The Avalanche (2nd) and the Blue Jackets (5th) both get their defensemen shooting. The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). Colorado has scored 4.15 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Blue Jackets, they have a leaky penalty kill (29th) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). Columbus has scored 2.45 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Blue Jackets hound the puck, but the Avalanche sit back.

Nathan MacKinnon (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 13 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL. Artturi Lehkonen (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (7 G / 4 A / 11 P in 11 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Charlie Coyle (1 G / 8 A / 9 P in 11 GP) isn’t far behind.

Scott Wedgewood (1-2-1 / .889 SV% in 4 GS) will likely start for Colorado. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-4-0 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) and Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Monahan and Garland out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Landeskog, Nelson and Roy. Elsewhere, the Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Blue Jackets do.

items.text: Valeri Nichushkin faces Colorado for the first time since leaving.
The Blue Jackets have been without Ivan Provorov all season.
Sean Monahan has four goals in six games against Colorado since 2023-24.
Artturi Lehkonen has ten goals on chances worth about 4.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
